questions.stem: Solve $x^4-5x^2+4=0$. Tap every solution on the number line.

hints.text: Each equation of the form $x^2=k$ with $k>0$ gives two solutions, one positive and one negative.
Solve each bracket separately: $x^2$ equals the number that makes that bracket zero.

pending_hints.text: Taking the square root gives both signs, so check each value has its partner.
pending_hints.why: The answer set {-2,-1,1,2} is symmetric, so the negative of any target is also a target. Flipping signs can never produce a wrong mark, so the predicate never fires meaningfully here. The hint's 'check each value has its partner' also nearly reveals the ± structure.

canonical_solution.text_md: Only $x^4$, $x^2$ and a constant appear, so treat $x^2$ as a chunk: $(x^2)^2-5x^2+4=0$.

questions.stem: Solve $x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$. Tap every solution on the number line.

hints.text: A cubic that factorises into three linear factors gives one solution from each factor. Check that every factor has a mark.
Set each factor equal to zero and solve it: a factor $(x+a)$ gives $x=-a$.

pending_hints.text: Substitute each marked value into $P(x)$; only values that give $0$ are solutions.
pending_hints.why: Fires if the student marks e.g. -2, 1, 3 and also 2. Substituting is valid, but the hint refers to $P(x)$, which the question never defines, so it may confuse the student. Not clearly helpful as written.

canonical_solution.text_md: Let $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-5x+6$. $P(1)=1-2-5+6=0$, so $(x-1)$ is a factor (Factor Theorem).
